name: Ulau-Suain
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page ulau1237 and langdoc complexquery bib (9 entries: Laycock 1973, Lean 1986, Laycock 1976, Ross 1988, Klaffl & Vormann 1905, Schmidt 1900-02, Ethnologue 2015, Erdweg 1901, Ray 1919; none typed grammar/phonology/sketch)
sources.note: Bibliographic only; Erdweg 1901 (Globus 79: 101-105, 'Ein Besuch bei den Varópu') typed listed by Glottolog as a wordlist with 'Sauvein = Ulau-Suain [svb]'.

sources.citation: Klaffl, Johann & Friedrich Vormann (mit Bemerkungen von W. Schmidt). 1905. Die Sprachen des Berlinhafen-Bezirks in Deutsch-Neuguinea. Mitteilungen des Seminars für Orientalische Sprachen zu Berlin 8 (Abt. I): 1-138. Part 3 'Der Ulau-Suen-Dialekt des Ali' (Klaffl), pp. 49-51, §§56-68; Schmidt comparative part §113a p. 74, §115b p. 76
sources.note: §57 'B. Lautverhältnisse' (p. 49) for Ulau-Suen lists vowels, diphthongs, consonants and phonotactics only; no accent sentence (verified on page scan and scanned). The accent rule 'Der Akzent liegt im allgemeinen auf der letzten Silbe' (p. 3) is stated for Ali, and p. 52 §70 repeats it for Tumleo ('wie im Ali'); neither the Jakamul nor the Ulau section repeats or refers to it. Schmidt's comparative part twice calls Ulau word-initial syllables unstressed: §113a p. 74 'Ulau hat, außer in den unbetonten Vorschlagsilben..'; §115b p. 76 'Besonders ist das der Fall in den (unbetonten) Vorsilben: ko…
sources.venue: Mitteilungen des Seminars für Orientalische Sprachen zu Berlin 8 (Abt

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia (Pacific Linguistics C-98). Canberra: ANU.http://hdl.handle.net/11858/00-001M-0000-0012-7B5D-4
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Schouten chapter pp. 120-132 uses Ross's own Ulau-Suain wordlist data (reflexes, pronominal paradigms) but gives no stress statement for Ulau-Suain; the only Schouten stress data (p. 86, ex. 3.114-3.115, lenition before stressed vowel) are Ali and Tumleo verb paradigms. p. 123: 'Detailed descriptions are available for Manam (Lichtenberk 1983) and Kairiru (Wivell 1981a, 1981b), and there is an early (but phonologically unreliable) sketch of Tumleo (Schultze 1911).'

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1976. Austronesian languages: Sepik Provinces. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2: Austronesian languages (Pacific Linguistics C-39), 399-418. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-C39.399
sources.note: Ulau-Suain entry no. 5, p. 405: 'Previous data confined to a brief word list by Erdweg (1901), and grammatical notes and a wordlist by Klaffl and Vormann (1905), who regard Ulau-Suain as a dialect of Ali - to which it stands moderately close.' Comparative wordlist pp. 411-418 gives Ulau-Suain forms without stress marks; nothing on stress.
sources.venue: New Guinea area languages and language study

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1976. History of research in Austronesian languages: Sepik Provinces. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), NGALLS vol. 2 (Pacific Linguistics C-39), 73-93. DOI 10.15144/PL-C39.73
sources.note: pp. 74-75: 'Klaffl adds thirteen pages on the "Ulau-Suen dialect of Ali"; it seems preferable nowadays, however, to regard Ulau-Suain as a separate language.. Virtually no new data on Ali or Ulau-Suain ever appeared.' Confirms Klaffl 1905 is the only descriptive text; nothing on stress.
